The earliest of the criteria is Tsai-Hill.

Outside the gauge section, Tsai-Hill is reached earlier, at 1.004 times the applied loading, at element 67, at the edge of a gripped tab: the clamped edge of a grip, where the stress grows as the mesh is refined, so it is reported apart from the answer.
As ASTM D3039/D3039M-17 reduces a test: the gross area is 36.58 mm² (25 by 1.463 mm), so the force along the coupon, 1.622e+04 N, is a stress of 443.5 MPa.

The extensometer over 25 mm reads 7289 microstrain, so the chord modulus between 1000 and 3000 microstrain is 60.85 GPa (laminate theory gives 60.85 GPa), and Poisson's ratio is 0.3152 (laminate theory: 0.3152); a linear model gives the same slope over any range.

By Tsai-Hill in the gauge section, the first ply fails at a gross stress of 458.3 MPa: a first-ply-failure stress, not the ultimate strength the standard takes at the maximum force of a test, which a linear model cannot give.
